lessons: Never repeat the hook line or question in the first 10-15 seconds; restating the setup (e.g., Potato Sprouts, Guardrails, Funny Bone) caused massive immediate drops between 23% and 32%.
Eliminate filler teaser lines that delay information (e.g., 'They are not just there to look cool', 'They look like similar fruits'), which lost over 30% of remaining viewers.
Do not include interactive pauses or countdowns like 'Pause and guess...'; these created consistent mid-video drop-offs (e.g., 400 Degree Foil, Maple Syrup).
Hook viewers using extreme counter-intuitive claims or historic/scale comparisons (e.g., 'older than the United States', space mystery beyond Pluto) to achieve loop/rewatch rates above 100%.
Lead with direct visual contrasts or paradoxes (e.g., tuna vs. cod meat color) to sustain high retention from start to end (vs_similar_end of 0.86).
worst_moment_types: Verbatim repetition of the hook line or title question
Interactive callouts or countdowns ('Pause and guess... three, two, one')
Vague transition/filler sentences that add no new facts
Stating obvious sensory setups instead of diving into the scientific cause
best_hook_types: Extreme comparative scale or historical facts ('older than the United States')
Challenging established baseline knowledge ('Pluto seemed like our solar system's edge...')
Direct visual paradoxes comparing two common things ('bluefin tuna and a cod... meat looks like two completely different animals')
